  reminder keeps the self shape (from == to) the wake policy needs to
  classify it exempt, so a chain survives a session-id change. Every
  lifecycle step lands in the receipt trail
  (`<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl`, `ScheduledReceiptLog`,
  best-effort): scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed
  (queue) and wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused (both hosts'
  wake paths; refusal receipts are once per refusal EPISODE — the latch
  lives in `InboxWakePolicy` next to the streak, so a held gate cannot
  spam the trail and a repeat episode after user input is receipted
  again).
  Sleep resilience (issue #259): all due math rides an injectable wall
  clock (`ScheduledMessageQueue(clock:)`), long waits are split into ≤60s
  timer legs (`maxTimerLeg`) that recompute the remaining delay from the
  wall clock on every fire — never accumulating duration drift — and
  hosts run a catch-up sweep at every TURN START (CLI `_beginUserPrompt`,
  app `sendText`) in addition to the idle inbox ticks, so the first
  post-sleep turn delivers every overdue record immediately. Catch-up is
  exactly-once per record (file removed on send + the `_delivering`
  in-flight guard) — missed cycles of a recurring self-re-arm are NOT
  replayed; the re-armed cycle simply resumes from "now". For true
  sleep-proofing (delivery DURING lid sleep) no in-process timer can
  help: add an external pinger, e.g. a cron/launchd entry that messages
  the session's mailbox — mail to an asleep session already launches a
  headless wake run that drains the inbox and sweeps due records.
 Failure isolation (issue #270): a throwing `send` is contained per
 record (logged via `onError` — CLI `[sched]` line, app `AppLog`), the
 record stays for the next sweep, and the post-failure re-arm floors the
 leg at `failureBackoff` (60s) so a poison record cannot spin a
 zero-delay timer; sweeps deliver in due-time order, and the app's
 turn-start sweep is awaited so the fresh turn sees the fired reminder.
 A failed SCAN (transient `listDir`/read error on a leg, gh-1180) is
 equally loud: `onError` + a `scan_failed` receipt, then a re-arm at
 `failureBackoff` — the arming heartbeat never silently disarms
 ("scan failed" used to be treated as "nothing pending", permanently
 disarming the scheduler with zero log). Corrupt record CONTENT is
 still skipped, not fatal (issue #59). Every lifecycle step is
 receipted to an append-only JSONL trail at
 `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`,
 gh-1180): `scheduled` / `delivered` (with lag) / `delivery_failed` /
 `scan_failed` from the queue, plus host-side `wake_attempted` /
 `turn_started` / `wake_refused` (with reason) from the CLI wake path —
 a post-mortem can distinguish "timer never fired" (no `delivered`)
 from "wake refused" without reading source. The trail is best-effort:
 a failing write logs via `onError` and never breaks scheduling.
 Records carry the scheduling instance's `owner` (mailbox prefix): a
 sweeper re-addresses a self-addressed record only when the stored owner
 matches its own prefix, and never deletes another instance's record -
 foreign-owned records are left where their owner sweeps (also across a
 root change: only own records migrate to an adopted folder's root).
 Legacy untagged records drain via the old any-sweeper path; records
 whose owner session is deleted (`/reset` mints a new id) stay on disk -
 there is no reaper, cleanup is manual. `agent_fabric` resolves the
 messages root lazily per sweep (was: pinned to the launch cwd at
 construction), and pending records migrate across a root change, so a
 session-folder adoption carries the reminders along instead of
 stranding them under the launch cwd.


  The `## Agent messaging` prompt section (prompts messaging_section.md, CLI +
  app variants) tells the model its own mailbox address. Turn-boundary
  delivery: `Agent.externalSteeringSource`
  merges inbox drains into the steering poll (main in AgentCli/AgentService
  as `_mainInboxMessages`, children via the executor) — messages land as
  sender-attributed user messages, so they persist in the session and read
  like a chat. Idle wake: an inbox watcher (2s CLI / 3s app) starts a turn
  when mail arrives while idle — two Fa instances chat live; a 10-run
  streak cap without user input breaks agent-to-agent ping-pong loops.
  The lanes live in `InboxWakePolicy` (gh-1180): user-kind mail always
  wakes and resets the streak (gating it would deadlock:
  no run → no reset → no run); a delivered `schedule_message`
  self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to) is EXEMPT from the
  cap — a deliberate agent-chosen cadence (night watch, periodic sweep)
  wakes forever, with a 30s cadence floor so a zero-delay re-schedule
  spin is still bounded like chatter; foreign agent chatter stays
  capped. A refused wake is never silent: one dim `[mail] wake refused`
  line per episode and a `wake_refused` receipt.
  UI: `/agents` rows show a `mail:N` pending marker (the CLI
  font has no ✉ glyph), the app's AgentsSection shows `✉N`; observe/detail
  views list the pending inbox.

# Daily auto-publish (issue #161): thin orchestrator over the existing
# publish channels. Each channel is an isolated leg — one leg failing never
# kills the others — and every failure self-files a deduplicated GitHub
# issue (label `bug`, assigned to the owner) that auto-closes when the leg
# goes green again. No publish logic is duplicated here: legs dispatch the
# existing workflows via `gh workflow run` and watch them.
#
#   testflight  build-mobile.yml   ios_content=all (the iOS half of the
#                                 mobile build)
#   play        build-mobile.yml   android_content=all,
#                                 android_track=beta (Android external
#                                 beta / open testing — issue #289 lifts
#                                 the standing "Android excluded" owner
#                                 decision for the release track; #947
#                                 adds the listing deploy — texts +
#                                 whole-set image replace + verify — so
#                                 the listing never trails the goldens;
#                                 the leg green-skips while the Play
#                                 secrets are absent)
#   pubdev      in-job OIDC publish, only when pubspec > pub.dev; otherwise
#               a green up-to-date check. The tag-time OIDC publish job
#               (ci.yml) stays the primary path; this leg is the catch-up +
#               loud-failure detector (e.g. expired publish credentials)
#   cli         build-macos.yml    desktop DMG + macOS CLI bundles +
#                                 extension, attached to the next-tag
#                                 release (version passed explicitly so
#                                 mobile/desktop never mint diverging tags)
#   website     pages.yml          fa1.dev (landing + web demo +
#                                 the /outlook add-in slice; gh-1684:
#                                 the extension zip moved to GitHub
#                                 Releases and is no longer site-hosted)
#   addin       office-addin.yml   manifest/taskpane acceptance suite; the
#                                 fa1.dev publish itself rides the website
#                                 leg (pages.yml assembles /outlook)
#
# Legs run only when main moved since the last GREEN daily run — skip-no-
# change is green-neutral, never red (#159 lesson). One exception (gh-1192):
# while main's pubspec version is not yet served by pub.dev the plan gate
# (scripts/daily_plan.sh) forces the legs anyway — a release-in-flight
# green must not become a skip baseline that stalls re-verification and
# rerun-recovery on a quiet main. Versioning stays the
# existing scheme: auto_release.sh patch-bumps + tags every main push
# (2h coalesce); the daily attaches mobile/desktop artifacts to the next
# tag and verifies/republishes pub.dev. See docs/ci.md.
#
# Pause: gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R IstiN/flutter_agent_harness

name: Daily auto-publish

run-name: "Daily auto-publish (${{ inputs.legs || 'all' }})"

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 5 * * *' # once daily, 05:17 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      legs:
        description: 'Leg(s) to run'
        type: choice
        default: all
        options:
          - all
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin
      force:
        description: 'Run even if main has not moved since the last green daily'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      inject_failure:
        description: 'TEST ONLY — fail this leg before any dispatch, to exercise the self-filing issue cycle'
        type: choice
        default: none
        options:
          - none
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin

permissions:
  contents: read

# One daily at a time; a queued run must not cancel an in-flight one.
concurrency:
  group: daily-publish
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  plan:
    name: Plan (change detection + versions)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # gh-1477: 10m was the same time bomb as the derive-version jobs — a
    # full-history fetch under a 10m ceiling. 20m + the blobless filter
    # below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    outputs:
      changed: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.changed }}
      next_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.next_tag }}
      latest_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.latest_tag }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.pubspec_version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: daily_plan.sh reads tags / commit metadata / one file
          # at origin/main — never historical blobs. Blobless keeps full
          # tag/commit metadata without the blobs (the full fetch outgrew
          # the old 10m ceiling in the twin derive-version job, run
          # 38027695551).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Detect main movement and derive versions
        id: plan
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          FORCE: ${{ inputs.force }}
        # gh-1192: the gate (baseline + the release-unresolved re-arm that
        # keeps AC1's «the next daily re-verifies» true on a quiet main)
        # lives in the extracted script — shell-harness tested by
        # test/release_flow_race_test.dart.
        run: bash scripts/daily_plan.sh

  # ── Dispatch legs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Shape per leg: dispatch the child workflow pinned to main, capture the
  # new run id, watch it, fail on any non-success conclusion. The child run
  # URL is exported even on failure so the report can excerpt its log.
  #
  # ── Timeout arithmetic (#351) ────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Invariants: watch budget > child worst-case (a legitimate slow child is
  # NEVER cancelled by the watcher — that was the #351 bug), leg
  # timeout > budget (the watcher, including its one cancel + re-dispatch
  # cycle, always outlives the child), and where the math fits under
  # GitHub's 360m job cap, leg timeout ≥ 2×budget + ~15m so the SECOND
  # wedge's fail-fast can actually fire inside the leg.
  #
  # Child worst-case = sum of the serialized job timeout-minutes along the
  # child's critical path (every job in a watched chain carries an explicit
  # timeout for exactly this). Margin = appear window (60×10s) + cancel
  # wait (180s) + poll slack ≈ 15m.
  #
  #   leg        child worst-case (serialized chain)          budget    leg timeout
  #   testflight version 20 → build-ios 90 → submit-ios 120   230m  →  250m (15000s) ; 360m
  #             (∥ release-mobile 15, covered by the max)
  #   play       version 20 → build-android 45 →              95m   →  110m (6600s) ; 240m
  #             submit-android 30 (∥ release-mobile 15)
  #   cli        version 20 → build-macos 150×2 (arm64 +      335m  →  350m (21000s) ; 360m
  #             x86_64 SERIALIZE on the single self-hosted
  #             runner) → release-macos 15
  #             (∥ cli matrix 45, extension 30 — shorter paths)
  #   (gh-1477: the version/plan jobs' ceiling moved 10 → 20m — a
  #   full-history fetch outgrew the 10m bomb; the fetch is now blobless
  #   and 20m is the seatbelt. Worst-cases and budgets grew by exactly
  #   the +10m.)
  #   website    pages build 45 → deploy 15                   60m   →   75m (4500s)  ; 180m
  #   addin      office-addin-suite 45 (single job)           45m   →   60m (3600s)  ; 150m
  #
  # Second-wedge headroom (2×budget + ~15m vs leg timeout): play 235 ≤
  # 240 ✓, website 163 ≤ 180 ✓, addin 133 ≤ 150 ✓. testflight (515 > 360)
  # and cli (715 > 360) CANNOT fit two full budgets under GitHub's 360m
  # job cap — their first wedge still self-heals (cancel at budget +
  # re-dispatch ≈ budget+13m), and a second wedge is bounded by the leg
  # timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast; both children carry
  # per-job server-side timeouts (#344) so a wedged job self-fails even
  # without the watcher.
  #
  # gh-172 (run 39374894901, 2026-10-20): the re-dispatched testflight
  # child sat queued FOREVER on the zombie self-hosted worker (a job-level
  # timeout is enforced BY the runner, so a hung worker outlives its own
  # 90m ceiling and never processes the run cancel either) — the leg burned
  # its remaining ~107m watching a child that could never start and died as
  # a bare 360m ceiling kill. The watcher now also treats "not completed
  # but NO job in_progress for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (default
  # max(600, budget/8) — 15000s/8 = 1875s ≈ 31m here; it cannot tell a
  # zombie-held pool from a sibling leg's job legitimately occupying the
  # shared fa-m5-1, so it waits out realistic sibling occupancy)" as a
  # wedge riding the same one self-heal, and cancels the child on the fail
  # path so an orphaned queued run can't publish unattended when the pool
  # revives. Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg
  # (testflight ≈ 250m + 13m + 31m stall = 294m < 360m).

  testflight:
    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 230m (version 20 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120) → budget 250m; 360m leg > budget. Two full budgets
    # (515m) exceed GitHub's 360m cap — a second wedge is bounded by this
    # leg timeout, not the watcher fail-fast.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'testflight')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'testflight'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=testflight) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (issues #343/#344): correlates OUR run by the
          # child's run-name ("build-mobile (none/all)" — displayTitle is
          # the only distinguisher in the run-list API), newest match in a
          # tight window; a wedged run (self-hosted slot lost, #344) is
          # cancelled and re-dispatched once before failing.
          # Budget 250m = child worst-case 230m (version 20 + build-ios 90
          # + submit-ios 120, #351; gh-1477 moved the version ceiling
          # 10 → 20m — blobless fetch + seatbelt) + 20m margin — a healthy
          # slow TestFlight
          # submit (Apple processing can legitimately take the full 90m
          # ASC wait + 15m verify) is never cancelled by the watcher.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (none/all)' \
            --budget-seconds 15000 \
            -f android_content=none -f ios_content=all \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  play:
    name: 'Leg: Play (Android external beta)'
    # Independent of the testflight leg (#359). The #348 serialization was
    # a mitigation for the #343 sibling-dispatch race; #351 eliminated that
    # race structurally — exact displayTitle correlation (this leg's child
    # runs as "build-mobile (all/none)", the testflight leg's as
    # "(none/all)"), NEWEST match, a tight 30s window, and build-mobile's
    # per-run_id concurrency group (no dispatch can cancel another). With
    # the race gone the needs-edge only bought harm: a cancelled testflight
    # watcher skipped Play behind it and the edge added up to 360m of start
    # latency (one leg's external blocker stopped the train — run
    # 34827074052, BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL user-owned).
    #
    # The two residual #346 concerns are handled structurally, not by
    # ordering:
    #   * same-tag convergence — both children independently derive
    #     latest-tag+1, so they can attach to ONE release concurrently;
    #     release_attach_or_create.sh is race-idempotent (a lost create
    #     uploads into the winner's release) with an ownership-scoped draft
    #     guard, and the asset sets never collide (AAB vs IPA).
    #   * runner contention — none: the Android chain is all GitHub-hosted
    #     runners; only build-ios touches the single self-hosted macOS
    #     runner (which already serializes physically with the cli leg's
    #     build-macos children — that pair has always been independent).
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic (unchanged by #359 — only the leg's START moved):
    # child wc 95m (version 20 + build-android 45 + submit-android 30) →
    # budget 110m; 240m leg ≥ 2×budget + 15m, so the second-wedge
    # fail-fast fits inside the leg.
    timeout-minutes: 240
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'play')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      # Secrets presence is checked in the first step — while the Play
      # upload keystore/service account are not configured, the leg green-
      # skips with a notice (existing neutral-skip leg semantics); it goes
      # live the moment the owner sets them (issue #289).
      PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON: ${{ secrets.PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON }}
      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
      ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
      ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'play'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=play) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Skip without Play secrets (green-neutral)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          missing=""
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD"
          if [ -z "${PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON:-}" ]; then
            missing="$missing PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON"
          fi
          if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
            echo "::notice::Play secrets not configured (missing:${missing}) — the Android leg skips green-neutrally until the upload keystore + Play service account secrets exist (issue #289 owner checklist)."
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "All Play secrets present — dispatching the Android build+upload."

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # all: build + Play upload + LISTING deploy (issue #947) — the
          # listing lane replaces the whole image set per locale + device
          # type and verifies it via edits.images.list, so the listing can
          # never trail the committed goldens by more than one train.
          # beta = the external/open testing track, mirroring the iOS leg's
          # external TestFlight group (#239 pattern).
          # Shared watcher (issues #343/#344). Since #359 the TestFlight
          # sibling leg fires CONCURRENTLY with this one (both needs: plan)
          # and dispatches the SAME workflow in the same minute —
          # correlation is by the child's run-name ("build-mobile
          # (all/none)" vs the sibling's "(none/all)", pinned by
          # test), never by "first run in the window", with newest-match +
          # the 30s window; a wedged run is cancelled and re-dispatched
          # once (with the same distinct inputs → same distinct title).
          # Budget 110m = child worst-case 95m (#351: version 20 +
          # build-android 45 + submit-android 30; the #947 listing
          # deploy rides the submit-android job's slack; gh-1477 moved
          # the version ceiling 10 → 20m) + 15m margin.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (all/none)' \
            --budget-seconds 6600 \
            -f android_content=all -f android_track=beta -f ios_content=none \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  cli:
    name: 'Leg: CLI + macOS desktop'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 335m (version 20 + build-macos 150×2 — the
    # arm64 AND x86_64 matrix legs SERIALIZE on the single self-hosted
    # macOS runner — + release-macos 15) → budget 350m; 360m leg > budget.
    # Two full budgets (715m) far exceed GitHub's 360m cap — a second
    # wedge is bounded by this leg timeout, not the watcher fail-fast
    # (both build-macos jobs carry 150m server-side timeouts, #344).
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'cli')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'cli'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=cli) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-macos.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Children derive version themselves (latest tag + 1 at their own
          # dispatch moment) — a tag pinned here would race auto_release and
          # could attach assets to a tag pointing at a different commit.
          # Shared watcher (issues #343/#344): correlates OUR run by the
          # child's run-name ("build-macos (create_release=true)") so a
          # concurrent human dispatch is never adopted; a wedged self-hosted
          # run is cancelled and re-dispatched once. Budget 350m = child
          # worst-case 335m (#351: version 20 + build-macos 150 ×2 arches
          # serialized on the one self-hosted runner + release-macos 15;
          # gh-1477 moved the version ceiling 10 → 20m)
          # + 15m margin.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-macos.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-macos (create_release=true)' \
            --budget-seconds 21000 \
            -f create_release=true \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  website:
    name: 'Leg: Website'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 60m (pages build 45 + deploy 15) → budget
    # 75m; 180m leg ≥ 2×budget + 15m, so the second-wedge fail-fast fits
    # (the old 45m leg made the self-heal dead code: 40m budget + 10m
    # appear window never completed inside it).
    timeout-minutes: 180
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'website')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'website'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=website) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      # pages.yml is path-filtered on push, so routine pushes (e.g. lib/
      # changes outside its filters) never redeploy — the daily guarantees
      # fa1.dev tracks main.
      - name: Dispatch pages.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (issues #343/#344). pages.yml takes no inputs, so
          # there is no displayTitle to disambiguate on — the watcher falls
          # back to newest-in-tight-window, and still bounds the watch
          # (cancel + one re-dispatch) instead of blocking forever.
          # Budget 75m = child worst-case 60m (#351: pages build 45 +
          # deploy 15) + 15m margin.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh pages.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --budget-seconds 4500 \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  addin:
    name: 'Leg: Outlook add-in'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 45m (single office-addin-suite job) →
    # budget 60m; 150m leg ≥ 2×budget + 15m, so the second-wedge fail-fast
    # fits (the old 45m leg made the self-heal dead code).
    timeout-minutes: 150
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'addin')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'addin'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=addin) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      # Acceptance suite (manifest validation, dart2js taskpane, Node +
      # Playwright e2e). The fa1.dev /outlook publish itself rides the
      # website leg — pages.yml assembles the same add-in into the deploy.
      - name: Dispatch office-addin.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (issues #343/#344). No inputs to disambiguate on
          # (newest-in-tight-window fallback), watch bounded at 60m =
          # child worst-case 45m (#351) + 15m margin.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh office-addin.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --budget-seconds 3600 \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  # ── pub.dev leg ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job (pub.dev trusted publishing
  # only accepts OIDC from tag-push runs — a schedule/dispatch run can never
  # satisfy it). This leg VERIFIES pub.dev serves the pubspec version and,
  # when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push publish run —
  # a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims, so the real
  # publish path retries. Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an
  # issue with a manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.
  # gh-1192: a tag-publish still EXECUTING (tag pushed, ci run not visible
  # yet or queued/in_progress, tag younger than the grace window) is
  # classified «release in flight» by scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh —
  # a neutral skip (no error, no auto-filed issue); the next scheduled
  # daily re-verifies. The 2026-10-03 collision fired the old «no ci.yml
  # run» error one minute before the healthy run completed (#1189, false
  # alarm). gh-1522: the version under test is the LATEST REMOTE TAG (the
  # committed pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder), so the «tag not cut
  # yet» state no longer exists.

  pubdev:
    name: 'Leg: pub.dev'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write # gh run rerun of the tag-publish run
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'pubdev')
    outputs:
      status: ${{ steps.check.outputs.status }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pubspec }}
      published_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.published }}
      run_url: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'pubdev'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=pubdev) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing published"
          exit 1

      # gh-1561: the never-triggered self-heal re-pushes the latest tag with
      # the fa-release-bot App token — a GITHUB_TOKEN push can never cascade
      # (gh-1172), the App's push can (the same mechanism ci.yml's release
      # job uses to cut tags). Job-scoped, expires with the job; this job's
      # own GITHUB_TOKEN stays read-scoped (job-level permissions block).
      # Shape mirrors the validator-proven precedent (ci.yml release job,
      # the create-github-app-token step): NO `if:` at all — secrets
      # context in a step-if trips GitHub's workflow validator; and a mint
      # on an unconfigured App (forks, rotation gap) fails, is SWALLOWED by
      # continue-on-error, outputs.token stays empty, and the script's
      # manual-re-push alarm fires exactly as before this change.
      # Least privilege, verified against the PINNED action (v3.2.0,
      # bcd2ba49 — review thread 10): the composite `permissions` input
      # does NOT exist there (action.yml defines only the generated
      # `permission-*` inputs — GitHub warns `Unexpected input(s)
      # 'permissions'` and the action never reads it; ci.yml:3980 rides
      # that warning). The HONORED ceiling is the granular
      # `permission-contents` input, which the action turns into the mint
      # request's permissions map: contents:write only — the tag re-push —
      # instead of the installation's full grant set. Without it the token
      # inherits every permission the fa-release-bot installation has.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3.3.0
        id: app-token
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          permission-contents: write

      - name: Verify pub.dev serves the pubspec version
        id: check
        # gh-1192: the classification (up-to-date / release-in-flight /
        # recovered + the unchanged alarms) lives in the extracted script so
        # it is shell-harness testable (test/release_flow_race_test.dart).
        # RELEASE_APP_TOKEN is empty when the mint above skipped (App not
        # configured) — the script then fails over to the manual-re-push
        # alarm instead of attempting a re-arm.
        env:
          RELEASE_APP_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh

  # ── Release-draft sweeper (issue #282) ────────────────────────────────────
  # Hygiene leg: no pipeline step may leave a draft release behind (the
  # 3-week-old v0.1.190 rot). The per-job guards in build-macos/build-mobile
  # own the failure path; this sweeper is the daily backstop — anything that
  # slips through (a cancelled run, a path without a guard) is deleted after
  # 24h and a deduplicated self-closing issue names the creating run so a
  # RECURRING stuck draft points at its broken step instead of rotting.
  # Runs on every daily (and manual) invocation regardless of leg results —
  # change-gating must not gate hygiene.
  sweep-drafts:
    name: Sweep stale release drafts
    needs: plan
    if: always() # even when plan failed or all legs skipped
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write # delete draft releases
      actions: read # name each swept draft's creating run (gh run list 403s without it, review of #294)
      issues: write # deduplicated self-closing sweep issue
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Delete drafts older than 24h and file the dedup issue
        run: bash scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh

  # ── Report + self-healing issues ─────────────────────────────────────────
  report:
    name: Summary + self-filed issues
    needs: [plan, testflight, play, pubdev, cli, website, addin]
    if: always() # runs even when plan failed, so plan failures enter the self-healing loop too
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
      issues: write
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Job summary table and issue lifecycle
        env:
          NEXT_TAG: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.next_tag }}
          PLAN_RESULT: ${{ needs.plan.result }}
          DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE: ai-teammate
          LEG_TESTFLIGHT: ${{ needs.testflight.result }}
          LEG_TESTFLIGHT_URL: ${{ needs.testflight.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_PLAY: ${{ needs.play.result }}
          LEG_PLAY_URL: ${{ needs.play.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_PUBDEV: ${{ needs.pubdev.result }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_STATUS: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.status }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_PUBSPEC: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.pubspec_version }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_PUBLISHED: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.published_version }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_URL: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_CLI: ${{ needs.cli.result }}
          LEG_CLI_URL: ${{ needs.cli.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_WEBSITE: ${{ needs.website.result }}
          LEG_WEBSITE_URL: ${{ needs.website.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_ADDIN: ${{ needs.addin.result }}
          LEG_ADDIN_URL: ${{ needs.addin.outputs.run_url }}
        run: bash scripts/daily_publish_report.sh

      # gh-1478: the inject_failure TEST hook must prove the filed digest
      # QUOTES the injected ::error:: line (signal-first excerpt via the
      # per-job log endpoint), not merely that an issue exists — the #1473
      # tree-noise regression class.
      # The `!= ''` guard matters: on schedule triggers the `inputs` context
      # is EMPTY (the dispatch `default: none` does not apply), so gating
      # only on `!= 'none'` would run — and fail — this step every cron run.
      - name: Verify injected-failure excerpt (TEST)
        if: always() && inputs.inject_failure != '' && inputs.inject_failure != 'none'
        env:
          INJECTED: ${{ inputs.inject_failure }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          title="[daily-publish] ${INJECTED} leg failed"
          n=$(gh issue list --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --state open \
                --label daily-publish --limit 200 \
                --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' \
                | while IFS=$'\t' read -r num t; do
                    [ "$t" = "$title" ] && echo "$num"
                  done | head -1)
          if [ -z "$n" ]; then
            echo "::error::inject_failure verify: no open issue titled '${title}' — the self-filing path regressed"
            exit 1
          fi
          text=$(gh issue view "$n" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
                   --json body,comments --jq '.body, (.comments[]?.body // empty)')
          if ! grep -qF "injected failure (inject_failure=${INJECTED})" <<< "$text"; then
            echo "::error::inject_failure verify: issue #${n} never quotes the injected ::error:: line — the signal-first excerpt regressed (gh-1478)"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "inject_failure verify OK: issue #${n} quotes the injected error line (gh-1478)"

content.text:
name: Build macOS Release (Fa)

# Issue #343: the daily-publish CLI leg and a human can dispatch this
# workflow in the same window; the run-name embeds the input so the
# watcher's displayTitle match (the only distinguisher in the run-list
# API) never adopts someone else's run.
run-name: "build-macos (create_release=${{ inputs.create_release }})"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version (e.g. v0.0.2) or "auto" to increment patch'
        required: false
        default: 'auto'
      create_release:
        description: 'Create GitHub Release'
        required: false
        default: 'true'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'true'
          - 'false'

# Release builds are never preempted (issue #194 pt 5, same principle as
# ci.yml: tag/release runs must not be cancelled mid-flight; gh-1537
# retired the post-merge main ci run).
concurrency:
  group: Build macOS Release (Fa)-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

# SEC-08 (#796): minimal default — release-attaching jobs grant
# contents: write in their own job-level blocks.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  version:
    name: Derive version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Explicit ceiling so the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351)
    # has a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477:
    # 10m was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew its twin in
    # build-mobile (run 38027695551). 20m + the blobless filter below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Derive build version
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          INPUT="${{ inputs.version }}"
          if [ -z "$INPUT" ] || [ "$INPUT" = "auto" ]; then
            LATEST=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo "")
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi
          else
            TAG="$INPUT"
            [[ "$TAG" != v* ]] && TAG="v$TAG"
            echo "Using manual version: $TAG"
          fi
          VERSION_CLEAN="${TAG#v}"
          echo "version=$VERSION_CLEAN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

  build-macos:
    name: Build macOS ${{ matrix.arch }}
    needs: version
    # gh-1600 F-A: pin the ONE self-hosted macOS runner (fa-m5-1) via its
    # unique registration label — the generic [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]
    # list also matched the Linux self-hosted box's labels (same routing
    # bug that sent the build-mobile iOS jobs to Linux, gh-1600).
    runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]
    # Issue #239: TestFlight submit now waits for Apple processing (bounded,
    # default 90 min) + a ~1-min one-shot appearance probe AFTER the
    # build/notarize work (gh-1041: the blocking distribution wait moved to
    # the deferred store-appearance-check workflow) — the job ceiling must
    # cover the worst case, not just the build.
    timeout-minutes: 150
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        arch: [arm64, x86_64]
    permissions:
      contents: write
    env:
      # Workaround: force .NET (used by the runner) to use SocketsHttpHandler
      # instead of Apple's SSL APIs, avoiding "bad certificate format" errors
      # caused by corporate Zscaler/MDM certificates in the system keychain.
      DOTNET_SYSTEM_NET_HTTP_USESOCKETSHTTPHANDLER: "0"

    steps:
      # ── Prepare persistent local git mirrors ────────────────────────────────
      # gh-1644: the old inline single-shot logic died on the first network
      # hiccup — the recreate fell through to a full `git clone --mirror`
      # whose ~1 h transfer ended in "error: 2931 bytes of body are still
      # expected" (run 38855793382, exit 128). The shared script retries the
      # fetch with VISIBLE stderr, aborts stalled attempts, and recreates
      # BLOBLESS (--filter=blob:none, the gh-1477 precedent) with retries and
      # partial-dir cleanup. Contract: scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh
      # gh-1665 review: this step runs BEFORE any checkout on persistent
      # self-hosted runners — the workspace may hold a pre-merge tree (or be
      # wiped), so the script is bootstrapped from the commit-pinned raw URL
      # (workflow_dispatch-only workflows ⇒ ${{ github.sha }} is always a
      # pushed commit) with the mirror copy as the no-network fallback.
      - name: Update local git mirrors
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR_BASE="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror"
          mkdir -p "$MIRROR_BASE"
          MIRROR="$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          SCRIPT="$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
          RAW="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/${{ github.sha }}/scripts/update_git_mirror.sh"
          if ! curl -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 "$RAW" -o "$SCRIPT" \
             || [ ! -s "$SCRIPT" ]; then
            echo "raw bootstrap failed — syncing the mirror and falling back to its copy" >&2
            # gh-1665 review (returned IMPORTANT): in the one-run-wide
            # first-post-merge window the persistent mirror is still a
            # PRE-MERGE tree. Cheap single-shot ensure (bounded resilience
            # stays owned by $SCRIPT below) so the extraction that follows
            # succeeds on any runner that can reach github.com at all —
            # raw.githubusercontent.com being down degrades to the
            # fallback instead of a red leg.
            if [ -d "$MIRROR" ] && git -C "$MIRROR" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              git -C "$MIRROR" fetch origin || true
            else
              rm -rf "$MIRROR"
              git clone --mirror https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR" || true
            fi
            BRANCH="$(git --git-dir="$MIRROR" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo main)"
            git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show "$BRANCH:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh" > "$SCRIPT" \
              || { echo "::error::could not bootstrap update_git_mirror.sh (raw URL unreachable and mirror lacks the script)" >&2; exit 1; }
          fi
          bash "$SCRIPT" \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git \
            "$MIRROR"

      # ── Checkout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # gh-1600 AC2: hardened mirror-checkout — the bare `rm -rf
      # "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` used to fail the whole checkout on stale
      # unremovable leftovers in the persistent shared workspace (bench
      # docker leftovers, jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/). Log-and-prune clean +
      # clone-around-stub; the per-arch build cache is parked outside the
      # workspace before the clean and restored after the clone (best-effort:
      # a lost cache re-builds from scratch, it never fails the checkout).
      # INLINE (not a composite action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...`
      # actions resolve against $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time — on this box
      # that is the PREVIOUS run's tree, and this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirrors
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          MIRROR_BASE="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror"
          MAIN_MIRROR="$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          ARCH="${{ matrix.arch }}"
          BUILD_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/build-cache/macos-$ARCH"

          echo "HOME=$HOME"
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MAIN_MIRROR=$MAIN_MIRROR"
          echo "ARCH=$ARCH"

          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" ]; then
            echo "Preserving existing macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            rm -rf "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mkdir -p "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/" \
              || echo "::warning::could not park the $ARCH build cache — it will be rebuilt from scratch (gh-1600)"
          fi

          cd /tmp

          # gh-1600 AC2: tolerate stale unremovable paths in the persistent
          # shared workspace — log-and-prune, never fail the checkout.
          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # gh-1600 rework (review thread): best-effort prune of previous
            # sidecars BEFORE creating a new one — the containers that held
            # them may have died since, so the retry often succeeds. On
            # this persistent box the runner's own _temp cleanup cannot
            # remove mount-held content either; without the prune every
            # degraded checkout would leave another timestamped dir behind
            # (unbounded growth until manual cleanup).
            rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          git clone --reference "$MAIN_MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                # gh-1600 rework (review thread): fresh content must win —
                # park the stale stub in the same $STALE sidecar and move
                # the fresh entry in. The old path skipped the fresh entry
                # (warning-only) and the trailing rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
                # then DELETED it, silently keeping the stale leftover at
                # that repo path. Skip-with-warning remains only as the
                # last-resort fallback when even parking the stub fails.
                STALE_DIR="${STALE:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-sidecar}"
                if mkdir -p "$STALE_DIR" 2>/dev/null && mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" "$STALE_DIR/" 2>/dev/null; then
                  mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
                else
                  echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
                fi
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          if [ -d "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/macos" ]; then
            echo "Restoring macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            rm -rf build/macos 2>/dev/null || true
            mkdir -p build
            mv "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/macos" build/ \
              || echo "::warning::could not restore the $ARCH build cache — it will be rebuilt from scratch (gh-1600)"
          fi

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): same rationale as
      # build-mobile.yml — on a persistent self-hosted runner the
      # flutter-action cache costs a ~1GB untar on setup plus a whole-SDK
      # re-tar POST per job. The composite action pins the SDK at
      # ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk (.fah-version marker):
      # subsecond reuse, one download per pin bump, no POST step.
      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install instead of the runner's
      # pre-installed SDK — the candidate-path loop picked up a stale
      # 3.44.4 at ~/.local/flutter, which broke `flutter pub get` the
      # moment the repo floor moved to >=3.47.0 (daily-publish #260/#261).
      - name: Setup Flutter environment
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-flutter-selfhosted
        with:
          # EXACT patch pin (#1431): this leg builds + gates fa-extension.zip
          # against scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv — a wildcard pin
          # re-resolves a new engine build on every 3.47.x patch and moves
          # the canvaskit/skwasm rev-hash dir the gate tracks. Bump
          # consciously, with any floor reseed in the same PR.
          flutter-version: '3.47.7'

      - name: Setup host toolchains
        run: |
          echo "/opt/homebrew/opt/ruby/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          echo "/opt/homebrew/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          flutter --version
          dart --version

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        run: |
          if command -v rustup &> /dev/null; then
            echo "Rust already installed"
            rustup show
          else
            echo "Installing Rust..."
            curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y
            source "$HOME/.cargo/env"
          fi
          echo "$HOME/.cargo/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          rustup --version
          cargo --version

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # The plist is gitignored, so the fresh CI checkout has none and the
      # native Firebase SDK logs I-COR000012/0008 at startup. Inject it from
      # a secret when available (same dev.fa1.app registration as
      # firebase_options.dart).
      - name: Write GoogleService-Info.plist (macOS)
        env:
          GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64" | base64 --decode > flutter_app/macos/Runner/GoogleService-Info.plist
            echo "GoogleService-Info.plist written (bundle: $(plutil -extract BUNDLE_ID raw flutter_app/macos/Runner/GoogleService-Info.plist))"
          else
            echo "⚠️ GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64 not set — building without the native Firebase plist"
          fi

      - name: Install Flutter dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: Dependency versions
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          echo "=== Dependency versions ==="
          flutter pub deps --style=compact

      # flutter_gemma ≥1.5.5 no longer downloads the Apple LiteRT-LM companion
      # dylibs from its hook (they are bundled via the Podfile phase), so a
      # fresh runner has nothing at ~/Library/Caches/flutter_gemma and the
      # Runner script phase fails with "Could not find macOS companion
      # dylibs". Seed the cache from the upstream native release (pinned,
      # sha256-verified).
      - name: Ensure flutter_gemma macOS companion dylibs
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          GEMMA_CACHE="$HOME/Library/Caches/flutter_gemma/native/macos_arm64"
          if [ -f "$GEMMA_CACHE/libGemmaModelConstraintProvider.dylib" ]; then
            echo "companion dylibs already cached"
          else
            echo "seeding companion dylibs from flutter_gemma native-v0.16.0"
            mkdir -p "$GEMMA_CACHE"
            # --retry alone skips transient mid-transfer resets (curl 56);
            # --retry-all-errors retries them (sha256 below guards corruption)
            curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 10 --max-time 600 \
              -o /tmp/litertlm-macos_arm64.tar.gz \
              https://github.com/DenisovAV/flutter_gemma/releases/download/native-v0.16.0/litertlm-macos_arm64.tar.gz
            echo "c597554a7a5cdf099658227099a54ef4916c5802b9182757e656e1788f9426b6  /tmp/litertlm-macos_arm64.tar.gz" | shasum -a 256 -c -
            tar xzf /tmp/litertlm-macos_arm64.tar.gz -C "$GEMMA_CACHE"
          fi
          ls -la "$GEMMA_CACHE"

      # The workspace is re-cloned every run, which wipes Pods/ and forces a
      # full pod install (~4 min with Firebase). Cache it keyed by the
      # lockfile; $HOME-level caches (pub-cache, CocoaPods download cache,
      # Ruby gems, Flutter SDK) already persist on the self-hosted runner.
      - name: Cache CocoaPods (macOS)
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: flutter_app/macos/Pods
          key: macos-pods-${{ hashFiles('flutter_app/macos/Podfile.lock') }}

      - name: Generate build info
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          GIT_COMMIT=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
          GIT_BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
          SUBMODULES=$(git submodule status --recursive | tr '\n' ';')

          mkdir -p lib/core/services
          printf '%s\n' \
            '// Generated build info — CI overwrites this file before compilation.' \
            '// ignore_for_file: constant_identifier_names' \
            '' \
            "const String kBuildGitCommit = '${GIT_COMMIT}';" \
            "const String kBuildGitBranch = '${GIT_BRANCH}';" \
            "const String kBuildSubmodules = '${SUBMODULES}';" \
            > lib/core/services/build_info.dart

          echo "Build info generated:"
          cat lib/core/services/build_info.dart

      - name: Cache vendored WasmRun macOS framework
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework
          key: wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0
      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 20
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git. Order of preference:
          # 1) actions/cache hit (keyed by the release tag) — warm until the
          #    repo's daily cache churn LRU-evicts the entry (saved 10-20
          #    06:02Z, gone by 10-21 19:03Z: gh-1759 ran cold twice);
          # 2) local working copy on this self-hosted runner;
          # 3) upstream release asset — the curl budget MUST fit the step
          #    cap WITH CORRECT ARITHMETIC (gh-1149): retries live in THIS
          #    bash loop, not curl --retry (which adds N MORE attempts AND
          #    restarts+truncates instead of resuming). Worst case with the
          #    gh-1759 budget: 4 × 240s max-time + 3 × 5s sleeps = 975s,
          #    + connect + unzip + slack ≈ 1035s < the 20-min (1200s) cap.
          #
          #    gh-1759: the gh-1149 budget (3 × 240s) was sized for this
          #    link's good-day ~300KB/s. The 10-21 daily run measured
          #    40–108KB/s (cold cache, both arch jobs): 3 × 240s banked
          #    only 29.5MB (x86_64) / 73% (arm64) of the 97,238,501-byte
          #    asset and the leg went red. Resume worked (`Resuming
          #    transfer from byte position …` in the logs) — the wire
          #    budget was simply too small, and the old pre-loop wipe
          #    threw each run's partial away, so a slow-link day never
          #    banked durable progress and the leg could not self-heal.
          #    Fixes: (a) the per-arch /tmp partial now PERSISTS across
          #    runs — -C - resumes it within the step AND across daily
          #    runs (macOS prunes only 3-day-untouched /tmp files; a daily
          #    run touches it) until the asset completes and the
          #    actions/cache post-step saves the framework; (b) the loop
          #    grew to 4 × 240s under a 20-min step cap.
          LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks"
          # PER-ARCH zip path: both matrix archs run on ONE self-hosted
          # runner (the shared-state race this file already guards with
          # per-arch keychains below) — a shared arch-less /tmp zip would
          # let one job's cleanup unlink the other's in-flight partial,
          # then both curls interleave bytes into one path.
          ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"
          # The release asset is immutable per tag — pin its digest so a
          # wrong-content-but-valid-zip cannot slip past unzip CRC32 into
          # the permanent wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0 cache (same pattern
          # as the litertlm download above). The pinned byte size tells a
          # truncated download (KEEP the partial — the next run resumes
          # it) apart from a complete-but-wrong one (PURGE and restart).
          ASSET_DIGEST="aca903d732202bcdf9c8d19fbb8a795c3c930762419f852a5ee228468c548a98"
          ASSET_BYTES=97238501
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          if [ -f "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework/Info.plist" ]; then
            echo "Using framework already in place (actions/cache hit or valid leftover)"
          elif [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
            echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
            cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
          else
            echo "No cache, no local copy — downloading from upstream release..."
            # The partial is deliberately NOT deleted between runs
            # (gh-1759): it is exactly what -C - is for. If the persisted
            # zip is already complete AND digest-valid, skip the download
            # — a -C - attempt against a complete file gets HTTP 416 and
            # reads success as failure.
            if [ -f "$ZIP" ] && echo "$ASSET_DIGEST  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c - >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "Complete, digest-valid $ZIP persisted from an earlier run — skipping download"
            else
              for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
                # --fail: without it curl exits 0 on HTTP 404/5xx and writes
                # the error page into the zip; with it every HTTP error
                # engages this loop's retries. -C - makes each attempt
                # RESUME the partial zip (Range requests), so slow links
                # make forward progress within this step AND across runs.
                if curl --fail -L -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
                  -o "$ZIP" \
                  https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip; then
                  break
                fi
                if [ "$attempt" = "4" ]; then
                  echo "download attempt $attempt failed — out of loop attempts" >&2
                else
                  echo "download attempt $attempt failed, resuming in 5s..."
                  sleep 5
                fi
              done
              got=$(wc -c < "$ZIP" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || echo 0)
              if [ "$got" -eq "$ASSET_BYTES" ] && echo "$ASSET_DIGEST  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -; then
                : # complete and authentic — fall through to unzip
              elif [ "$got" -lt "$ASSET_BYTES" ]; then
                echo "WasmRun.xcframework.zip incomplete: $got / $ASSET_BYTES bytes after $attempt attempts — keeping the partial; the next run resumes from byte $got (gh-1759)" >&2
                exit 1
              else
                echo "WasmRun.xcframework.zip is $got bytes (expected $ASSET_BYTES) or failed its pinned sha256 — purging it so the next run restarts clean" >&2
                rm -f "$ZIP"
                exit 1
              fi
            fi
            unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"
          fi
          ls -la "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"

      # Per-arch keychain: both matrix archs build on ONE self-hosted
      # runner; a shared build.keychain raced (one job's delete+create
      # emptied it under the other's codesign — errSecInternalComponent /
      # "No certificate found", builds 86).
      - name: Import macOS signing certificate
        id: signing
        env:
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64 }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
          MACOS_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID }}
          MACOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.MACOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "⚠️  No signing certificate found — building unsigned (development only)"
            echo "signed=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          else
            echo "✅ Signing certificate found — importing..."
            security delete-keychain build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain 2>/dev/null || true
            security create-keychain -p "$MACOS_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain
            security default-keychain -s build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain
            security unlock-keychain -p "$MACOS_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain
            security set-keychain-settings -t 3600 -u build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain
            security list-keychains -d user -s build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db

            echo "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64" | base64 --decode > certificate.p12
            security import certificate.p12 -k build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain \
              -P "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD" \
              -T /usr/bin/codesign \
              -T /usr/bin/productbuild
            security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple: -s -k "$MACOS_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain
            echo "signed=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi

          if [ -n "$MACOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$MACOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64" | base64 --decode > profile.provisionprofile
            echo "profile_embedded=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

            # Make the profile visible to Xcode manual signing.
            PROFILE_UUID=$(security cms -D -i profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract UUID raw -)
            PROFILE_NAME=$(security cms -D -i profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract Name raw -)
            PROFILE_TEAM=$(security cms -D -i profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract TeamIdentifier.0 raw - 2>/dev/null || true)
            echo "Profile: $PROFILE_NAME / UUID: $PROFILE_UUID / team: $PROFILE_TEAM"
            mkdir -p "$HOME/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning Profiles"
            cp profile.provisionprofile "$HOME/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning Profiles/${PROFILE_UUID}.provisionprofile"
            echo "profile_uuid=$PROFILE_UUID" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "profile_team=$PROFILE_TEAM" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          else
            echo "⚠️  No provisioning profile found — TestFlight will warn"
            echo "profile_embedded=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi

      - name: Build macOS release (${{ matrix.arch }})
        env:
          BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
          BUILD_VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID }}
          MACOS_NOTARIZE_TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_NOTARIZE_TEAM_ID }}
          PROFILE_UUID: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.profile_uuid }}
          PROFILE_TEAM: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.profile_team }}
        run: |
          ARCH="${{ matrix.arch }}"
          echo "Building for architecture: $ARCH"
          cd flutter_app
          if [ -n "${MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID:-}" ]; then
            export FA_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID"
            export FA_CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual
            if [ -n "${MACOS_NOTARIZE_TEAM_ID:-}" ]; then
              export FA_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$MACOS_NOTARIZE_TEAM_ID"
            elif [ -n "${PROFILE_TEAM:-}" ]; then
              export FA_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$PROFILE_TEAM"
            fi
            if [ -n "${PROFILE_UUID:-}" ]; then
              export FA_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER="$PROFILE_UUID"
            fi
          else
            export FA_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="-"
            export FA_CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic
          fi
          FLUTTER_XCODE_ARCHS="$ARCH" flutter build macos --release \
            --build-name=$BUILD_VERSION \
            --build-number=$BUILD_NUMBER
          MAIN_BIN=$(find build/macos/Build/Products/Release/Fa.app -name "Fa" -type f | head -1)
          echo "=== Binary architecture verification ==="
          echo "Binary path: $MAIN_BIN"
          file "$MAIN_BIN"
          lipo -info "$MAIN_BIN"
          echo "=== End binary verification ==="
          # The Dart side resolves the wasm_run FFI surface via dlsym on the
          # main executable. If the symbols were dead-stripped or not exported
          # the app boots to a white screen on TestFlight — fail here instead.
          echo "=== wasm_run FFI symbol verification ==="
          # dyld_info reads the exports trie, which survives stripping
          # (nm -gD fails on stripped binaries with "no dynamic symbol table").
          EXPORTS=$(xcrun dyld_info -exports "$MAIN_BIN" 2>/dev/null || true)
          WIRE_COUNT=$(echo "$EXPORTS" | grep -c " _wire_" || true)
          echo "wasm_run wire_* exports in binary: $WIRE_COUNT"
          for SYM in _wire_compile_wasm _store_dart_post_cobject _init_frb_dart_api_dl; do
            if ! echo "$EXPORTS" | grep -qE " ${SYM}\$"; then
              echo "::error::$SYM is not exported from the app binary — wasm_run would crash at runtime (white screen)"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          echo "✅ wasm_run FFI symbols are exported"

      - name: Package as DMG
        id: package
        env:
          SIGNED: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.signed }}
          PROFILE_EMBEDDED: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.profile_embedded }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          ARCH="${{ matrix.arch }}"
          APP_PATH="flutter_app/build/macos/Build/Products/Release/Fa.app"
          DMG_NAME="fa-macos-${ARCH}-${VERSION}.dmg"

          # Size diet (#1096 AC4 + direction 3): drop what no macOS code path
          # can load — before any codesign so the seal covers the shipped
          # tree. Both cuts ride in flutter_assets inside App.framework:
          # 1) assets/wasm (~47 MB) — WASI interpreter modules loaded
          #    exclusively via WasiSandboxShell (env_factory_io.dart routes
          #    desktops to the host Process shell; every rootBundle.load of
          #    assets/wasm lives in the mobile-only shell).
          # 2) packages/js_widget_runtime/test — the pub package's
          #    own test fixture (coach_anny.glb, 5.6 MB); nothing in the app
          #    references that path (the live model, when used, is fetched
          #    by the JS-app catalog, not bundled).
          ASSETS="$APP_PATH/Contents/Frameworks/App.framework/Versions/A/Resources/flutter_assets"
          # Shared prune (scripts/prune_flutter_assets.sh — the same call
          # runs on the no-sandbox build and every web packaging surface):
          # fails loudly if the flutter_assets layout drifts instead of
          # silently shipping the fat bundle. Re-enable path (review,
          # #1096): if a desktop WASI/sandbox mode ever ships
          # (WasiSandboxShell on macOS), reseed assets/wasm — until then a
          # desktop wasm load would fail as a missing asset, not a
          # #1224-class "no lazy loader" stub.
          bash scripts/prune_flutter_assets.sh "$ASSETS" \
            assets/wasm packages/js_widget_runtime/test

          rm -f fa-macos-*.dmg tmp-fa.dmg
          rm -rf dmg-staging

          echo "Packaging: $APP_PATH → $DMG_NAME (arch: $ARCH)"

          if [ "$SIGNED" = "true" ] && [ -n "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID" ]; then
            echo "Signing .app bundle..."

            RESVG_BIN="$APP_PATH/Contents/Resources/resvg"
            if [ -f "$RESVG_BIN" ]; then
              echo "Stripping extended attributes from resvg..."
              xattr -cr "$RESVG_BIN" 2>/dev/null || true
              echo "Signing resvg binary..."
              codesign --force --sign "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID" \
                --options runtime \
                --timestamp \
                "$RESVG_BIN"
            fi

            find "$APP_PATH" -type f \( -perm +111 -o -name '*.dylib' \) | while read -r bin; do
              if codesign -dv "$bin" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID"; then
                continue
              fi
              echo "Signing nested binary: $bin"
              codesign --force --sign "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID" \
                --options runtime \
                --timestamp \
                "$bin" 2>/dev/null || true
            done

            if [ "$PROFILE_EMBEDDED" = "true" ] && [ -f "profile.provisionprofile" ]; then
              echo "Embedding provisioning profile..."
              cp profile.provisionprofile "$APP_PATH/Contents/embedded.provisionprofile"
              APP_ID=$(security cms -D -i profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract Entitlements xml1 -o - - | grep -A 1 'com.apple.application-identifier' | tail -1 | sed 's/.*<string>\(.*\)<\/string>.*/\1/')
              TEAM_ID="${APP_ID%%.*}"
              # Start from Release.entitlements (network client+server, file
              # bookmarks, calendar, contacts, health, homekit, audio input)
              # and inject the provisioning identity keys — do NOT collapse

=== VENDORED.md ===
# flutter_inappwebview_macos (vendored)

Verbatim copy of the published `flutter_inappwebview_macos` **1.2.0-beta.3**
(pub.dev, MIT — see `LICENSE`), required by the coherent
`flutter_inappwebview` 6.2.0-beta.3 set (gh-1235).

**Single change vs upstream** (both macOS deployment-floor declarations
raised from 10.14 to 14.0, the app's own minimum):

- `macos/flutter_inappwebview_macos/Package.swift` — `.macOS("10.14")` → `.macOS("14.0")`
- `macos/flutter_inappwebview_macos.podspec` — `s.platform = :osx, '10.14'` → `'14.0'`

Why: upstream declares a 10.14 floor, but
`Sources/flutter_inappwebview_macos/WebAuthenticationSession/WebAuthenticationSession.swift`
marks `presentationAnchor(for:)` `@available(macOS 10.15, *)`, so the
`ASWebAuthenticationPresentationContextProviding` conformance fails to compile
at the 10.14 target (both the SwiftPM and the CocoaPods path). Upstream
master still carries the bug — no fixed release or commit to pin to, hence
the vendor.

**Drop procedure**: once upstream releases a version whose Package.swift /
podspec minimum is ≥ 10.15, delete this directory and the
`flutter_inappwebview_macos` entry in
`flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` `dependency_overrides`.

content.thinking:
So `buildMacOS` flow:
1. Migrations run (incl. SPM integration migration — adds package refs to pbxproj).
2. `validatePluginSupport`.
3. `projectInfo` (xcodebuild -list).
4. `buildSettingsForBuildInfo` (xcodebuild -showBuildSettings).
5. `updateGeneratedXcodeProperties`.
6. **`updateMinimumDeployment`** — bumps the ephemeral Package.swift from 12.0 → 14.0 IF buildSettings has MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET > 12.0 AND manifest exists.

WAIT — but where does the ephemeral Package.swift get CREATED in this flow?? `generatePluginsSwiftPackage` (which writes Package.swift) is called from `setUp` (DarwinDependencyManagement) — which is called from `injectPlugins` — which runs in... `flutter_project.ensureReadyForPlatformSpecificTooling` → happens in the `build` command BEFORE `buildMacOS`. Let me verify: in `commands/build.dart` or `assemble.dart`: `await project.ensureReadyForPlatformSpecificTooling(...)` → `refreshPlugins` → `injectPlugins(...)` → setUp → generatePluginsSwiftPackage → creates Package.swift (platform 12.0 default).

So by the time `updateMinimumDeployment` runs in buildMacOS, the manifest EXISTS (12.0) and gets bumped to 14.0. On Xcode 26 this worked (green 10-22). On Xcode 27 it apparently didn't (12.0 at build).

Why? `buildSettings['MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET']` — from step 4 `xcodebuild -showBuildSettings -scheme Runner -configuration Release -sdk macosx`. Under Xcode 27, could this have returned 12.0?? Where would 12.0 come from at showBuildSettings time... PROJECT-LEVEL settings! The project-level build config list (33CC10E82044A3C6003C045) — let me check if it sets MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET. Earlier awk output showed project-level section without deployment target; the three 14.0s are: Flutter Asemble Profile (line 620?), Runner Debug (844), Runner Release (894)? Wait the earlier awk output mapping was confusing. Let me re-derive precisely which configs have the 14.0 lines: lines 620, 844, 894.

From the awk (lines 530-930): 
- 535 isa XCBuildConfiguration (Pods-RunnerTests.debug → name Debug) — RunnerTests has baseConfigurationReference Pods-RunnerTests... hmm wait, those Pods-RunnerTests xconfigs — the Pods project adds base configs to RunnerTests AFTER pod install; but in the REPO, the pbxproj... let me look directly.

Let me just dump each XCBuildConfiguration block with its id, name, and whether it has MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET.

arguments.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
p = 'flutter_app/macos/Runner.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj'
text = open(p).read()
# find all XCBuildConfiguration blocks
blocks = re.findall(r'\t\t([0-9A-F]{24}) /\* (.+?) \*/ = \{\n\t\t\tisa = XCBuildConfiguration;.*?\n\t\t\};', text, re.S)
ids = re.findall(r'\t\t([0-9A-F]{24}) /\* (Debug|Release|Profile) \*/ = \{', text)
print("config ids + names:")
for i,n in ids: print(' ', i, n)
# map configuration-list membership
for m in re.finditer(r'\t\t([0-9A-F]{24}) /\* Build configuration list for (PBXNativeTarget|PBXAggregateTarget|PBXProject) "(.+?)" \*/ = \{\n\t\t\tisa = XCConfigurationList;\n\t\t\tbuildConfigurations = \(\n((?:.*\n)*?)\t\t\t\);', text):
    print("LIST", m.group(3), "->", ", ".join(re.findall(r'([0-9A-F]{24})', m.group(4))))
# which blocks set MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET
for m in re.finditer(r'\t\t([0-9A-F]{24}) /\* (\w+) \*/ = \{\n\t\t\tisa = XCBuildConfiguration;\n(.*?)(?=\n\t\t\};)', text, re.S):
    has = 'MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET' in m.group(3)
    val = re.search(r'MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET = ([^;]+);', m.group(3))
    print(m.group(1), m.group(2), 'DEPLOY=', val.group(1) if val else None)
EOF

3. Is there a project-level knob the flutter tool reads for the SPM package floor? `updateMinimumDeployment(project:, platform:, deploymentTarget:)` — the deploymentTarget is read from buildSettings of the Runner scheme. So the ONLY input is the resolved build setting.
